metadata.name: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0
metadata.issuing_body: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
metadata.description: The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0 provides guidance to industry, government agencies, and other organizations to manage cybersecurity risks. CSF 2.0 adds a sixth function, GOVERN, alongside the original five: IDENTIFY, PROTECT, DETECT, RESPOND, RECOVER.

requirements.title: Govern — Organizational Context: Mission Understanding
requirements.description: The organizational mission is understood and informs cybersecurity risk management decisions.
requirements.guidance: Align cybersecurity strategy with organizational mission. Document risk appetite and tolerance levels.

requirements.title: Govern — Risk Management Strategy: Risk Tolerance
requirements.description: Risk management objectives are established and agreed to by organizational stakeholders.
requirements.guidance: Define and document organizational risk tolerance. Review with senior leadership annually.

requirements.title: Identify — Asset Management: Software Inventory
requirements.description: Inventories of hardware managed by the organization are maintained.
requirements.guidance: Maintain automated asset discovery and inventory. Include cloud workloads and AI systems.

requirements.title: Identify — Risk Assessment: Vulnerabilities Identified
requirements.description: Vulnerabilities in assets are identified, validated, and recorded.
requirements.guidance: Run authenticated vulnerability scans. Validate and prioritise findings. Track remediation to closure.

requirements.title: Protect — Identity Management and Authentication: Identities and Credentials
requirements.description: Identities and credentials for authorized users, services, and hardware are managed by the organization.
requirements.guidance: Implement centralised identity management. Enforce MFA. Automate credential lifecycle.

requirements.title: Protect — Identity Management and Authentication: Access Permissions
requirements.description: Access permissions, entitlements, and authorizations are defined in a policy, managed, enforced, and reviewed, and incorporate the principles of least privilege and separation of duties.
requirements.guidance: Enforce least privilege and separation of duties. Conduct quarterly access certification reviews.

requirements.title: Protect — Data Security: Data-at-Rest Protection
requirements.description: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-at-rest are protected.
requirements.guidance: Encrypt data at rest using AES-256 or equivalent. Manage encryption keys centrally.

requirements.title: Protect — Data Security: Data-in-Transit Protection
requirements.description: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-in-transit are protected.
requirements.guidance: Enforce TLS 1.2+ for all in-transit data. Disable weak cipher suites. Monitor certificate expiry.

requirements.title: Protect — Technology Infrastructure Resilience: Network Integrity
requirements.description: Networks and environments are protected from unauthorized logical access and usage.
requirements.guidance: Segment networks by sensitivity zone. Deploy intrusion prevention. Monitor East-West traffic.

requirements.title: Detect — Continuous Monitoring: Network Monitoring
requirements.description: Networks and network services are monitored to find potentially adverse events.
requirements.guidance: Deploy network detection and response (NDR). Baseline normal traffic. Alert on anomalies.

requirements.title: Detect — Adverse Event Analysis: Anomaly Investigation
requirements.description: Potentially adverse events are analyzed to better characterize the events and detect cybersecurity incidents.
requirements.guidance: Establish SOC triage procedures. Define MTTD and MTTR targets. Use threat intelligence to enrich alerts.

requirements.title: Respond — Incident Management: Incident Execution
requirements.description: The incident response plan is executed in coordination with relevant third parties once an incident is declared.
requirements.guidance: Maintain and test incident response plan annually. Define communication trees. Run tabletop exercises.

requirements.title: Recover — Incident Recovery Plan Execution
requirements.description: The recovery portion of the incident response plan is executed once initiated from the incident response process.
requirements.guidance: Define RTO and RPO. Test backup and restore procedures quarterly. Document recovery lessons learned.
